# Module 8 Knowledge Check

This knowledge check covers the key learning outcomes from Module 8: Share Your Results. Test your understanding of experimental design, data interpretation, and scientific communication.

## Question 1: Experimental Design Review

When designing your capstone experiment, what is the most important consideration?

- [ ] Using the most expensive equipment available
- [ ] Formulating a clear research question that connects to your earlier experiments and can be answered with available methods
- [ ] Conducting as many replicates as possible
- [ ] Choosing the most difficult procedure


## Question 2: Reproducibility and Consistency

Throughout this course, you have repeated techniques multiple times. Why is this emphasis on reproducibility important?

- [ ] To waste time
- [ ] To demonstrate that your results are reliable and not due to chance; consistent results indicate sound technique and methodology
- [ ] Because lab time must be filled
- [ ] Only the first attempt is scientifically valid


## Question 3: Integrating Multiple Data Types

Your capstone project involves phenotypic (Biolog), growth curve, and genomic data. Why integrate all three data types?

- [ ] To confuse readers
- [ ] To provide multiple independent lines of evidence supporting your conclusions; different data types answer different questions about your isolate
- [ ] They are redundant; only one is necessary
- [ ] To increase the page count of your report


## Question 4: Communicating Scientific Results

What is the primary audience for scientific communication of your results?

- [ ] Only your instructor
- [ ] Other researchers and educators who need to understand your findings and methods to evaluate and build upon your work
- [ ] Only people in your lab
- [ ] Social media followers


## Question 5: Limitations and Future Directions

An important part of scientific communication is discussing limitations of your study. Which of the following is a valid limitation?

- [ ] The experiment was hard to do
- [ ] We only tested three carbon sources instead of all 94; conclusions may not apply to other conditions
- [ ] We didn't have enough time
- [ ] The technique was not interesting


## Question 6: Linking Results to Broader Concepts

Throughout this course, you have studied microbial metabolism, genomics, and interactions. When presenting your capstone results, how should you connect them to these broader concepts?

- [ ] They should not be connected; focus only on your isolate
- [ ] Discuss how your isolate's characteristics fit into microbial biology, ecology, or biotechnology applications; explain why your findings matter beyond the lab
- [ ] Only discuss equipment used
- [ ] Connect to random topics


---

**Review these learning outcomes to deepen your understanding:**

- Review techniques, concepts, and experiments from the course
- Practice repeating experiments to improve consistency and reproducibility
- Describe the purpose, methods, and results of your designed experiment
- Interpret genomic data, including gene annotations and protein interaction predictions
- Analyze how your experiment contributes to your overall research goal

**Next Steps:** If you found any questions challenging, revisit the experimental design and scientific communication sections as you finalize your capstone project.
